summary: Fix MIDI/gate output timing when audio is rendered ahead (pre-existing 128-sample wrap), measure timing in the emulator before/after, verify once

r.model: The model is correct. routine_() only runs when doSomeOutputting() returns true, i.e. when the render buffer is empty. The TX buffer then holds exactly 128 - due unplayed samples. In the emulator each of around 11,000 windows started where the previous one ended (0 deviations, 0 underruns). The sample at position t plays 128 - due + t - movement after the timer start.
r.before:
Base, timer as planned (TGRA) against the moment the DMA reaches the window sample:
- Normal playback: 192 runs, all between -1.2 and +0.2 samples. With 16-sample windows nothing wraps around.
- When saving: 97 runs, 25 of them at -128 samples, i.e. 2.9 ms too early. Affected are the MIDI clocks that lie later in the 64-sample window (31% of the clocks with t>0).
r.after: Normal playback: 192 runs, all between -1.2 and +0.1 samples. When saving: 97 runs, all between -1.4 and +0.2 samples, no outliers at -128, although 29 of them needed more than 128 samples of lead time. The saved XML is identical (same sha256).
r.change:
In audio_engine.cpp, scheduleMidiGateOutISR(): s = 128 + t - due - (movement & 127).
- If s <= 0 and t >= 0, there is an underrun, and s is increased by 128, as before.
- If s <= 0 and t < 0, the sample has already played, and s becomes 1.
- The special cases -1 → 0 and the gate's minimum off time stay.
- New: s is limited to at most 5605, so that the 16-bit TGRA does not overflow.
- Formatted with clang-format, no new warnings.
r.howToRun: MIDI=1 ./run.sh <tree|elf> [out] in /home/user/deluge/mastertune-1.2.1/tests/song, takes about 2 to 3 minutes. The results are in out/midi-play/midi_timing.json and out/midi-save/midi_timing.json. MIDI_SYNTHS, MIDI_BARS and MIDI_SAVE_BARS can be set. It also works directly with song_emu.py --midi-timing, optionally together with --save-while-playing.
r.notes:
- Harness rework: blockcount.c got deadlines for interrupts. song_emu.py now models the timer (MTU2 channel 2) and the MIDI UART (DMA, 16-byte FIFO, 31250 baud) with interrupts, plays in real time like the task manager and saves repeatedly. make_sd.py has the option --midi-track; the default song stays bit-identical. Everything is documented in the header of run.sh.
- Separate finding: Song::renderAudio() disables the interrupts per output (DISABLE_ALL_INTERRUPTS). The timer interrupt therefore actually comes up to 33 samples (normal) or 41 samples (when saving) too late, the same in base and fix.
- The timer constant 515616 instead of 520833 Hz makes up around 1%, about -1 sample.
- Gate outputs were not tested, because the song has no CV track.
- Nothing is committed in /home/user/deluge.

v.reproduced: Remeasured with MIDI=1 run.sh, midi-base.elf against midi-fix2.elf (the same file as build/Release). When saving, 25 of 97 timer runs in the base are at -128; with the fix all are between -1.4 and +0.2. In normal playback both are between -1.2 and +0.2, and the sha256 is the same. The model is correct: routine_() only runs with an empty render buffer, and doSomeOutputting() never writes past saddr. So the formula also holds modularly with an underrun. Checked and fine: t<0→1, clamp 5605, gate minimum off time, external clock, no song (t=0 computes as before). The formula itself is correct; nothing gets worse in normal playback.

problems.problem: TCNT_2 is never set to 0 before the timer starts. The MTU2 clears TCNT on the compare match and keeps counting until the ISR stops the timer. While Song::renderAudio() disables the interrupts, that is up to 465 counts. The next run comes early by this remainder. If TGRA is smaller than the remainder, it only fires after the 16-bit overflow, around 127 ms too late. The new path s=1 (TGRA 11) almost always runs into this overflow.
problems.evidence: Harness copy with the TCNT model: scratchpad/h/song_emu.py, logs scratchpad/tbase.log and tfix.log. Remainder above 40 counts in 110/193 runs (normal) and 41/97 (saving), at most 376 and 451 respectively. Planned time: normal, in base and fix, up to -32 samples; when saving with the fix, up to -38. Base when saving: timer up to +5408 samples (123 ms) too late, clocks on the wire up to +811.
problems.fix: Set *TCNT[TIMER_MIDI_GATE_OUTPUT] = 0; directly before enableTimer() (the timer is stopped there). After that the previous harness model with a start at 0 applies, i.e. -1.4 to +0.2. The TCNT model also belongs in song_emu.py.

problems.problem: Notes go out around 2.5 ms before the audio: if a clock falls on the note tick, doMIDIClockOutTick() flushes the buffer immediately. This existed before; the fix does not change it. The harness only measures clocks. Also, it never resets MidiTiming.source after an interrupt, so the attribution 'UART transfer-end' is wrong.
problems.evidence: Note status bytes against sample 0 of their window, base the same as fix: -60 to -119 samples, median -107 (normal) and -116 (saving). Logs: scratchpad/nbase.log, nfix.log.
problems.fix: Tackle separately: send notes via the timer like clocks instead of flushing immediately, or deliberately keep the behavior. In the harness, reset source after returning from the ISR and measure notes as well.
